primary_reason: Nebius reported rapid AI-cloud revenue growth, more than $40 billion of customer commitments, materially expanded contracted-power plans, and strong customer prepayments, but the build-out remains extremely capital intensive and direct point-in-time valuation is not verified in this slow baseline.
strongest_counter_case: Q2 operating cash flow was dominated by customer prepayments while capital expenditures materially exceeded operating cash flow; the company also used equity, pre-funded warrants, convertibles, and secured debt, and it did not disclose a complete quantitative customer-concentration schedule. Execution delays, GPU or power constraints, contract repricing, dilution, or weaker customer prepayments could therefore impair the capacity ramp before it produces durable free cash flow.
invalidation: Official evidence shows a material cancellation, repricing, delay, or non-renewal of the large contracted AI-cloud commitments.
Verified liquidity, customer prepayments, and financing sources no longer cover the disclosed capacity build-out without materially adverse solvency or dilution risk.
Official evidence shows that GPU availability, power delivery, or data-center construction cannot support the announced capacity ramp.
A validated point-in-time valuation packet shows that expected capacity and cash-flow growth cannot justify the observed enterprise value under conservative assumptions.
next_review_trigger: A validated point-in-time NBIS valuation packet using a completed-session market snapshot and current diluted share count.
The next official earnings release and filed financial statements.
A new official disclosure of customer concentration, contract economics, financing, dilution, GPU supply, power delivery, or data-center commissioning.
